symbols.k: the number of clusters (the k in k-means); the Gaussian count in a mixture
symbols.K: the number of clusters; also the number of components or eigenfaces kept
symbols.i: counts data points (instances), one at a time
symbols.j: counts clusters, or Gaussians in the mixture
symbols.n: the number of features (columns of the data matrix); some sections reuse n, see the table of letters
symbols.x: a data point: its list of feature values (a single number in the 1-D EM examples)
symbols.C: a cluster, meaning a set of points; the whole clustering is a list of these
symbols.a: the silhouette's a(i): point i's average distance to the others in its own cluster
symbols.b: the silhouette's b(i): point i's average distance to the nearest other cluster
symbols.P: the partition: which cluster each point is in (P_i is point i's cluster); elsewhere a probability
symbols.d: the distance between two items (Euclidean in k-means); d_ki is a distance between clusters
symbols.c: a centroid: the centre (mean) of a cluster; c_j belongs to cluster j
symbols.z: a hidden tag: how much of point i came from Gaussian j
symbols.sum: add up the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.mu: the mean (centre) of a Gaussian, one per cluster
symbols.h: the hypothesis: the current guess at the mixture's parameters (its means)
symbols.v: a direction to project onto (a unit vector); the best ones are eigenvectors
symbols.E: the expected value: the average over the unknown hidden values
symbols.sigma: the standard deviation of a Gaussian, how wide the bell curve is
symbols.s: the silhouette score s(i) of point i; in the gap rule, a standard deviation
symbols.lambda: an eigenvalue: how much the data spreads along its eigenvector (also the Lagrange multiplier)
symbols.N: the number of training images (eigenfaces); in the mixture, N(x; mu, sigma) is the Gaussian density
symbols.p: the mixing weight p_j: the chance that Gaussian j generates a point; also a probability density
symbols.gamma: a setting in the linkage update: the weight on the gap between the two old distances
symbols.alpha: a setting in the linkage update: the weight on one of the two old distances
symbols.F: the F-measure for comparing clusters to classes; inside FP and FN it means 'false'
symbols.T: 'true' in TP and TN: clustering and classes agree about the pair; in the 2x2 eigenvalue formula, the trace
symbols.e: Euler's number, the base of the exponential in the Gaussian formula
symbols.W: the within-cluster sum of squares: total squared distance from each point to its centre
symbols.Y: the complete data: the observed values plus the hidden tags
symbols.mid: given: the probability of what is on the left when what is on the right is known
symbols.X: the data: all instances, as a set or a table with one row per instance
symbols.min: the smallest of the values listed or shown under it
symbols.max: the largest of the values listed or shown under it
symbols.S: the diagonal matrix of eigenvalues, which says how much each new axis stretches
symbols.V: the matrix whose columns are the eigenvectors: the new axes
symbols.t: part of the transpose mark (flips a column into a row); in eigenfaces, also the query image
symbols.phi: an eigenface: an eigenvector of the face covariance matrix
symbols.y: the complete description of an instance; elsewhere a label or a second coordinate
symbols.abs: the size of a set (how many points it holds) or the absolute value of a difference
symbols.f: one of the two views of an instance in co-training
symbols.B: the number of random reference datasets in the gap statistic; also the second Gaussian, called B
symbols.in: is an element of, or lies in
symbols.R: recall: the share of truly-together pairs that the clustering also put together
symbols.Sigma: the covariance matrix of the face images
symbols.w: how much of eigenface k the centred query image contains
symbols.hat:x: the rebuilt input that the autoencoder's decoder produces from the code
symbols.norm: the length of the vector inside; squared, it is the squared distance between the two
symbols.D: the dissimilarity matrix: a table of distances between every pair of clusters
symbols.log: the logarithm of the quantity that follows
symbols.L: the Lagrangian: the quantity to maximise combined with its constraint
symbols.w:trace: the trace: the sum of a matrix's diagonal entries, equal to the total variance
symbols.w:cov: the covariance: how much two centred features move together
symbols.u: a second feature, paired with h when computing their covariance
symbols.I: the identity matrix: it leaves any vector unchanged
symbols.A: the first Gaussian in the two-Gaussian example, called A
symbols.infty: infinity: a value growing without limit
symbols.w:rand: the Rand index: the share of pairs on which clustering and classes agree
symbols.w:jaccard: the Jaccard index: like Rand but ignoring pairs both keep apart
symbols.nabla: the gradient: how the quantity changes with each part of the vector shown
symbols.exp: e raised to the power that follows
symbols.l: counts the Gaussians in the sum on the bottom of the share formula
symbols.w:var: the variance: the spread of the values
symbols.w:gap: the gap statistic: how much tighter your clusters are than random data's

Clustering: the setup.n: the number of features per instance (the m by n matrix has n columns)
Clustering: the setup.C: one cluster, a subset of the points; the clustering is the list C of them

k-means clustering.E: the cost of a partition: the total distance from points to their centres
k-means clustering.P: the partition: P_i is the cluster that point i is assigned to

Mixture models and EM.n: counts the Gaussians in the bottom sum; for the covariance count, the number of attributes
Mixture models and EM.j: counts the Gaussians (clusters) in the mixture
Mixture models and EM.P: a probability, as in P(Y given h)
Mixture models and EM.p: in p(x given mu), how plausible the point is under that Gaussian; p_A, p_B are mixing weights
Mixture models and EM.B: the second Gaussian in the example, called B
Mixture models and EM.k: the number of Gaussians in the mixture

Hierarchical clustering.i: one of the two clusters being merged
Hierarchical clustering.j: the other of the two clusters being merged
Hierarchical clustering.k: some other cluster whose distance to the merged pair is needed
Hierarchical clustering.K: the number of clusters at which to stop merging
Hierarchical clustering.n: the number of points in a cluster (n_i for cluster i)
Hierarchical clustering.d: a distance between two clusters (d_ki is from cluster k to cluster i)
Hierarchical clustering.x: a data point, shown on the dendrogram

Choosing the number.k: the number of clusters being tried
Choosing the number.b: counts the random reference datasets, from 1 to B
Choosing the number.s: the standard deviation of the reference scores at that number of clusters
Choosing the number.W: the total within-cluster variation; W_k for your data, W_kb for reference set b

Evaluating clusters.i: the point whose silhouette is being scored
Evaluating clusters.s: the silhouette score of point i, between -1 and 1
Evaluating clusters.C: another cluster, whose average distance from point i is measured
Evaluating clusters.P: positive in TP and FP (clustering puts the pair together); alone, precision
Evaluating clusters.N: negative in FN and TN: the clustering keeps the pair apart
Evaluating clusters.F: 'false' in FP and FN: the clustering and the classes disagree on the pair; alone, the F-measure
Evaluating clusters.T: 'true' in TP and TN: the clustering and classes agree on the pair

Dimensionality reduction and PCA.n: the number of features in the m by n data matrix; in 1/n and 'n times the dropped eigenvalues', the number of instances
Dimensionality reduction and PCA.K: the number of top components kept
Dimensionality reduction and PCA.C: the covariance matrix: how each pair of features varies together
Dimensionality reduction and PCA.t: part of the transpose mark: flips a column vector into a row
Dimensionality reduction and PCA.h: one of two centred features whose covariance is taken

Eigenfaces.k: counts eigenfaces: how many are kept, or which one
Eigenfaces.K: the number of eigenfaces kept; in the nearest-neighbour step, the K of k-NN
Eigenfaces.n: the number of images, the same as N
Eigenfaces.d: the number of pixels in one image
Eigenfaces.X: the matrix of images, one image per column
Eigenfaces.c: marks the centred version (average image subtracted)
Eigenfaces.mu: the average face: the mean of all training images
Eigenfaces.a: how much of eigenface k a training image contains
Eigenfaces.t: the query (test) image; also part of the transpose mark
Eigenfaces.x: one image, as a long vector of pixel values

PCA alternatives.z: the code: the compressed features made by the encoder
PCA alternatives.x: the input that goes into the autoencoder

Semi-supervised learning.h: the classifier trained on the labelled data
Semi-supervised learning.f: one view (set of features) of an instance
Semi-supervised learning.x: the input features of an instance

Where the slides are loose.n: the number of images in eigenfaces (same as N); elsewhere a count of features
Where the slides are loose.z: the hidden tag: 0 or 1 in hard k-means, a probability in EM
Where the slides are loose.sigma: a Gaussian's standard deviation: shared in the short E step, sigma_j when each differs

Formula sheet.k: number of clusters in Gap(k); a third cluster in the linkage update; which eigenface in w_k
Formula sheet.K: the number of top components kept
Formula sheet.i: counts data points; in the linkage update, one of the two merged clusters
Formula sheet.j: counts clusters, Gaussians or components; in the linkage update, the other merged cluster
Formula sheet.n: instance count; n_i is a cluster's size; E step: component index; covariance count: attributes
Formula sheet.C: a cluster (C_j) in the centroid; the covariance matrix in the PCA rows
Formula sheet.a: the silhouette's a(i); in a_k, how much of eigenface k an image contains
Formula sheet.b: the silhouette's b(i); under the sum, counts reference datasets
Formula sheet.P: the partition (P_i); a probability in P(Y given h); precision in the F formula
Formula sheet.d: a distance; d_ki is the distance between clusters k and i
Formula sheet.c: a centroid c_j; in X_c, centred
Formula sheet.N: the normal (Gaussian) density in the mixture posterior
Formula sheet.T: 'true' in TP and TN; in the 2x2 eigenvalue formula, the trace
Formula sheet.F: the F-measure; in FP and FN, 'false'
Formula sheet.mu: a Gaussian's mean; in the eigenface rows, the average face
Formula sheet.h: the hypothesis (mixture parameters); in cov(h,u), a centred feature
Formula sheet.t: the query image; in v-transpose, part of the transpose mark
Formula sheet.s: the silhouette score s(i); in the gap rule, a standard deviation
Formula sheet.x: a data point; in the eigenface rows, an image
Formula sheet.e: Euler's number, the base of the exponential
Formula sheet.E: the expected value: the average over the hidden values
Formula sheet.w: how much of eigenface k the centred query contains

Exam traps.n: the number of instances, as in 1/n versus 1/(n-1)
Exam traps.Sigma: the covariance matrix of the face images

1. k-means by hand.c: as c_1 or c_2, a cluster centre; alone, the third example point (1, 2)
1. k-means by hand.W: the within-cluster sum of squares after the update

2. One EM iteration.e: Euler's number, the base of the exponential
2. One EM iteration.mu: the mean of one of the two Gaussians

5. PCA on four points.x: the first coordinate of a centred point
5. PCA on four points.y: the second coordinate of a centred point
5. PCA on four points.C: the covariance matrix of the centred points

6. External evaluation.a: a cluster label: the clustering named this cluster a
6. External evaluation.b: a cluster label: the clustering named this cluster b
6. External evaluation.P: 'positive' in TP and FP; alone, precision: the share of together-pairs that are right
6. External evaluation.R: recall: the share of truly together pairs that the clustering found
6. External evaluation.F: 'false' in FP and FN; alone, the F-measure
6. External evaluation.T: 'true': clustering and classes agree on the pair
6. External evaluation.N: negative: the clustering keeps the pair apart
